data.hypothesis: The selected parent combines four shared warp partials with two 64-bit warp-shuffle stages. Summing the four partials directly from shared memory in lane zero may remove those shuffle instructions, while trading them for four serial shared loads and a lane-zero-only branch. This tests a distinct final-aggregation path without changing the 128-thread mapping, one-element-per-lane input, recursive passes, or single CTA barrier; no speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: Same recursive 128-thread reduction workload; these are search measurements, not confirmation or attribution to a particular kernel stage.
memory_lessons.claim: The three distinct valid candidates measured 29.9853 μs (CUB), 30.6225 μs (selected two-shuffle parent), and 30.8038 μs (another shuffle variant), versus the baseline at 46.4832 μs. Their reported full-call means motivate a contrasting reduction experiment but do not establish a confirmed ordering or cause.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this direct shared-partial aggregation with the same correctness cases and repeated full-call protocol; seek confirmation before treating any search-time difference as an improvement.

data.notes: Selected parent and provenance retained: 3665f246711f422c. The candidate changes only the post-barrier assembly of four warp partials; the recursive global pass structure, scratch ping-pong, default-stream launches, and final asynchronous copy remain unchanged. The catalog reports three distinct valid programs and no repeats; its measurements are search results. This candidate has not been built, validated, or timed here; controller validation and repeated full-call comparison against baseline remain necessary.
transformations: Replace the final four-partial warp shuffle combination with a lane-zero-only sequential sum of the four shared warp partials after the existing CTA barrier.

Keep 64-bit per-lane and recursive intermediate accumulation, 128 threads, one input element per lane, recursive ceil(count/128) passes, caller-provided scratch, default-stream launches, and final asynchronous device-to-device copy.
